name: tabs
pattern: Single-select tabs following the WAI-ARIA APG Tabs Pattern
responsibility: Provides behavior, ARIA, keyboard interaction, and state outputs only; generates neither appearance nor content.

targets.tablist: Exactly one data-tabs-target="tablist" inside the root

authorMarkup.pairing: A valid pair consists of exactly one tab and one tabpanel inside the root sharing the same nonempty data-tabs-value, with the tab inside the sole tablist target. Duplicate values, a missing counterpart, zero or multiple tablists, and tabs outside the tablist invalidate the entire controller (contractValidation.invalidMarkup). Do not continue by excluding only invalid pairs.
authorMarkup.label: The consumer supplies the tablist aria-label, or may reference a label with an authored aria-labelledby.
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate elements or content.

semanticElements: Exactly one tablist target is required.
At least one tab target is required, and every tab must be a native <button type="button">. Validate type because an omitted type submits a form.
Every tab target must be a descendant of the tablist target.
Every tab and tabpanel needs a nonempty data-tabs-value, unique on each side and paired one-to-one. A missing counterpart is invalid.
orientation must be horizontal or vertical; activation must be automatic or manual. Typos are invalid rather than silently changing the interaction mode by falling back to a default.
Not validated: tabpanel position, mismatch between data-tabs-value-value and pairs (runtime state, handled by fallback), or the tablist accessible name.
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate on connection, target changes, and observed attribute changes. Invalid markup prevents structural, operational, and state-output writes, makes selection and public API operations (value setter and select) no-ops, and issues console.warn once per connection. Do not issue completion warnings. Ignore intermediate target-replacement states within one microtask. Reapply enhancement when markup becomes valid without warning again. Do not throw.
contractValidation.warning: Use the standard English disabling warning and describe the expected markup: one tablist, native <button type="button"> tabs, one-to-one pairs with unique nonempty data-tabs-value values, and supported orientation/activation values.

completion.warning: List completed attributes using "Added <attributes>. Include them in your markup." Warn once per connection using a flag separate from the enhancement-disabling warning.
completion.excluded: Tablist aria-orientation reflects the orientation value; tabpanel tabindex is required for controller operation. Neither is subject to completion warnings.

value.description: data-tabs-value of the initially selected pair
The selected data-tabs-value, or an empty string without selection. Assignment follows select(value) and remains synchronized with data-tabs-value-value.

select(value).description: Select a known, valid, enabled pair. Empty or unknown values, invalid pairings, and disabled tabs are no-ops.

tabs:beforechange.when: Before committing selection from pointer or keyboard interaction

detail.previousValue: The currently selected value, or an empty string without selection

tabs:beforechange.effect: preventDefault() prevents the selection change, but does not cancel keyboard-driven focus movement.

tabs:change.when: After committing selection from pointer or keyboard interaction

detail.previousValue: The value before the change, or an empty string without selection

events.programmatic: The value setter, select(value), initialization, dynamic fallback, and reconnection do not emit tabs:beforechange or tabs:change.
events.sameValue: Selecting the current pair through pointer or keyboard interaction does not emit tabs:beforechange or tabs:change.
events.nestedTabs: When listening on a root with nested tabs, use event.target === event.currentTarget, or :self in a Stimulus action, to exclude events from inner tabs.

initial: Select the pair referenced by data-tabs-value-value when that pair is valid and enabled.
Select the first enabled pair when the requested value is empty, unknown, invalidly paired, or disabled.
Without pairs or when all tabs are disabled, set value to an empty string and leave selection empty. Set every tab tabindex to -1 and hide every tabpanel.
selection.pointer: Clicking an enabled tab selects its pair with reason="pointer". Do not select disabled tabs.
selection.programmatic: The value setter and select(value) emit no events and preserve current selection for invalid requests.
dynamic: Preserve the selected pair while it remains valid and enabled.
Programmatically select the first enabled pair when the selected pair is removed, becomes invalid, or its tab becomes disabled.
Return to the initial no-selection state when no enabled pairs remain.
Adding a pair alone does not change the current value.
When no selection exists and a valid enabled pair is added or re-enabled, programmatically select the first enabled pair.

keyboard.focusModel: Use roving tabindex so Tab enters the tablist at the selected tab. Exclude disabled tabs from focus navigation.

horizontalLtr.ArrowLeft: Move to the previous enabled tab.
horizontalLtr.ArrowRight: Move to the next enabled tab.

horizontalRtl.ArrowLeft: Move to the next enabled tab.
horizontalRtl.ArrowRight: Move to the previous enabled tab.
horizontalRtl.directionSource: Use the tablist computed direction, including inherited direction.

vertical.ArrowUp: Move to the previous enabled tab.
vertical.ArrowDown: Move to the next enabled tab.

common.Home: Move to the first enabled tab.
common.End: Move to the last enabled tab.
common.wrap: Previous/next navigation wraps at both ends.

activation.automatic: Select with reason="keyboard" when focus moves.
activation.manual: Arrows, Home, and End move focus only; Enter or Space selects the focused tab with reason="keyboard".

tab: aria-controls referencing the corresponding tabpanel ID
tabpanel: aria-labelledby referencing the corresponding tab ID
tabindex="0" only when tabindex is absent

managedMarkup.preservation: Preserve existing IDs and authored attributes other than controller-owned state outputs. Authored role, aria-controls, aria-labelledby, or aria-orientation values conflicting with the contract violate the author contract and are outside the accessibility guarantee.
managedMarkup.generatedIds: Generated tab and tabpanel IDs must be unique within the document, including against authored IDs.
managedMarkup.disabled: Read the native tab disabled attribute; do not add data-* attributes for disabled state.

stateOutputs.ownership: The following attributes are controller-owned state outputs and are normalized to the selection, even when authored values exist.
stateOutputs.emptySelection: Put every tab in unselectedTab state and every tabpanel in unselectedPanel state.

lifecycle: Register event subscriptions in connect() and remove them in disconnect(). Do not duplicate them during Turbo reconnection.
Leave generated structural attributes and state outputs on disconnect().
Normalize structural attributes and state outputs against current markup and value on reconnection.

Track dynamic tablists, tabs, and tabpanels through tablistTargetConnected, tablistTargetDisconnected, tabTargetConnected, tabTargetDisconnected, tabpanelTargetConnected, and tabpanelTargetDisconnected.
Coalesce target and value callbacks into one reconciliation per microtask; do not run a queued reconciliation after root disconnect().
Observe tab disabled/type and tab/tabpanel data-tabs-value only while connected; stop the MutationObserver in disconnect().
Reflect runtime changes to data-tabs-value-value, orientation, and activation through Stimulus value callbacks.

blocking.item: Verify roles, names, selected state, tab/panel relationships, automatic/manual activation, and disabled-tab announcements
blocking.impact: The contract makes real-device verification an implementation completion requirement. Automated tests do not replace this result.
blocking.evidence: The maintainer confirmed completion of the Safari + VoiceOver checks listed here. This is a maintainer-reported real-device result, not a conclusion inferred from automated tests.

acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.

Controller behavior, ARIA, focus, and keyboard interaction must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA for conforming authored markup. Label contents, panel content, colors, focus indicators, layout, and other consumer-controlled appearance/content remain the consumer's responsibility.
Roles, names, relationships, aria-selected, focus, and keyboard interaction must agree with the WAI-ARIA APG single-select Tabs Pattern.
Preserve authored IDs. Generated IDs must not collide with document IDs or IDs from other tabs instances.
Keep value and the visible panel consistent for initialization, pointer, keyboard, public JS API, and dynamic fallback.
Tab aria-selected, tabindex, and data-state and panel hidden/data-state must always describe the same selection.
Invalid, unknown, or disabled programmatic values do nothing; programmatic changes emit no events.
User selection respects tabs:beforechange cancellation and emits tabs:change once only after commitment.
Repeated disconnect/reconnect must not duplicate listeners or increase event counts per user selection.
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

Real-device verification with macOS Safari and VoiceOver is an implementation completion requirement: verify roles, names, selected state, tab/panel relationships, automatic/manual activation, and disabled-tab announcements.
Report checks that have not been performed as unverified.
testMatrix: Roles, aria-controls, aria-labelledby, aria-orientation, and the tablist accessible name
Authored ID preservation, document-wide generated-ID uniqueness, and multiple instances
Valid, empty, unknown, and disabled initial values; all-disabled state. With valid markup, no selection occurs only when all pairs are disabled; missing pairs invalidate enhancement.
Automatic/manual selection, roving tabindex, Tab entry, Enter, Space, Home, End, and wrapping
Horizontal LTR, horizontal RTL, vertical mode, and no handling of ArrowUp/ArrowDown in horizontal mode
Shared roving_navigation behavior for empty length, negative indexes, unrelated keys, and LTR/RTL mapping
Skipping disabled tabs for pointer and keyboard interaction
tabs:beforechange/tabs:change order, detail, bubbling, cancellation, and pointer/keyboard reasons
Successful value setter/select(value), invalid-value no-ops, and no programmatic events
Pair addition/removal, disabled changes, selection preservation/fallback, and transitions to no selection
Turbo-equivalent disconnect/reconnect and prevention of duplicate listeners
Synchronization of aria-selected, tabindex, data-state, and hidden
Isolation of nested tabs events through event.target === event.currentTarget or :self
Engine-specific results for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Real-device macOS Safari and VoiceOver results

testMatrix.description: Missing completion attributes warn once per connection; complete markup does not warn.
Invalid markup warns once and disables enhancement; valid markup reapplies enhancement without repeating the warning.

mutation.description: Accept duplicates, missing counterparts, and tabs outside the tablist as valid.

negativeControls.expectedFailure: tabs-pair-validity fails, along with tabs-semantic-validation checking the same pair-validity invariant.

mutation.description: Make disabled tabs selectable. handleClick's tab.disabled check and requestSelection's enabledPairs are independent guards; removing only one is not detected. Remove both together.

negativeControls.expectedFailure: tabs-disabled-guard fails.

mutation.description: Remove document-wide ID collision checks. Per-document counter persistence and the do-while document.getElementById check are independent guards; removing only one is not detected. Remove both together.

negativeControls.expectedFailure: tabs-id-uniqueness and ID-uniqueness tests in callers sharing ensureElementId fail. Measurements include accordion-id-uniqueness, combobox-state-sync, listbox-id-uniqueness-negative, tabs-state-sync, and ensureElementId unit tests. ID uniqueness is shared across callers, so failure is not limited to one test. The counter and do-while are independent guards; the tabs test fails only when both are removed. The do-while-only mutation belongs to listbox-id-uniqueness-negative. editable-ids also fails because it checks the same shared-utility invariant.

mutation.description: Overwrite authored IDs.

negativeControls.expectedFailure: tabs-id-preservation and tests of callers sharing ensureElementId fail. The measured 19 tests cover combobox, dialog, dropdown-menu, listbox, password-field, splitter, tabs, and ensureElementId unit tests. Authored-ID preservation is a shared invariant, so failure is not limited to one test. This is the sole owner of the mutation breaking that guard. editable-ids also fails because it checks the same shared-utility invariant.
